mil5.2.4:0.4: 4. Question on Release from the Snare of Death
mil5.2.4:1.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, this too was said by the Blessed One:
mil5.2.4:2.1: ‘Not in the sky, not in the midst of the ocean,
mil5.2.4:2.2: Not by entering a mountain cave,
mil5.2.4:2.3: Is there found that place on earth
mil5.2.4:2.4: Where, standing, one could be freed from the snare of death.’
mil5.2.4:3.1: Yet the Blessed One also taught the protective discourses (paritta),
mil5.2.4:3.3: the Ratana Sutta, the Metta Sutta, the Khandha Paritta, the Mora Paritta, the Dhajagga Paritta, the Āṭānāṭiya Paritta, and the Aṅgulimāla Paritta.
mil5.2.4:3.4: If, Venerable Nāgasena, one is not freed from the snare of death even when gone into the sky, into the midst of the ocean, or into a palace, a hut, a cave, a grotto, an overhanging rock, a chasm, a hole, a mountain cleft or a gap between mountains, then the practice of protection is false.
mil5.2.4:3.5: But if release from the snare of death comes about through performing protection, then the statement ‘Not in the sky...
mil5.2.4:3.6: the snare of death’ is also false.
mil5.2.4:3.7: This too is a two-horned dilemma, a knot even tighter than a knot, that has come to you to be resolved by you.”
mil5.2.4:4.1: “Your majesty, the Blessed One did say ‘Not in the sky...
mil5.2.4:4.2: the snare of death,’ and he also taught the protective discourses. But the latter apply to one who has life remaining, who is of suitable age, and whose kamma is not an obstruction. For one whose life is exhausted, your majesty, there is no action or effort that can make them stay.
mil5.2.4:5.1: Take a dead tree, your majesty, withered and dry, without sap, its life ended, its life-formations gone: even if a thousand pots of water were poured on it, it would not become moist or put forth green shoots.
mil5.2.4:5.2: In just the same way, your majesty, for one whose life is exhausted, there is no action or effort of medicine or protection that can make them stay. Even the herbs and medicines of the earth, your majesty, are of no use to one whose life is exhausted.
mil5.2.4:5.3: But for one who has life remaining, who is of suitable age and free of the obstruction of kamma, protection guards and keeps them safe; it was for such a person that the Blessed One taught the protective discourses.
mil5.2.4:6.1: Just as, your majesty, a farmer would hold back water from fully ripened grain whose stalks are dead; but grain that is young, dark as a rain cloud, and of fitting age grows with an increase of water.
mil5.2.4:6.2: In just the same way, your majesty, the action of medicine and protection is set aside and rejected for one whose life is exhausted; but for those people who have life remaining and are of suitable age, protective discourses and medicines have been taught, and by them they flourish.”
mil5.2.4:7.1: “If, Venerable Nāgasena, one whose life is exhausted dies and one with life remaining lives, then protective discourses and medicines are pointless.”
mil5.2.4:7.2: “Your majesty, have you ever seen in the past any disease turned back by medicines?”
mil5.2.4:7.3: “Yes, venerable sir, I have seen hundreds.”
mil5.2.4:7.4: “Then, your majesty, the statement ‘The practice of protection and medicine is pointless’ is false.”
mil5.2.4:8.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, the efforts of physicians are visible: medicines are drunk and applied, and by their effort the disease is turned back.”
mil5.2.4:8.2: “When protective discourses are being recited, your majesty, the sound is heard, the tongue grows dry, the heart is moved, the throat becomes tired.
mil5.2.4:8.3: By that recitation all illnesses are calmed and all misfortunes depart.
mil5.2.4:9.1: Your majesty, have you ever seen anyone bitten by a snake who, by means of a spell, has the venom drawn out, made to flow out, and made to recede upward and downward?”
mil5.2.4:9.2: “Yes, venerable sir, that is still done in the world today.”
mil5.2.4:9.3: “Then, your majesty, the statement ‘The practice of protection and medicine is pointless’ is false.
mil5.2.4:9.4: For a snake that wishes to bite a person who has performed protection does not bite; it closes its open mouth. The raised clubs of robbers do not come down; they drop their clubs and show affection. A furious elephant comes up and calms down. A great blazing mass of fire approaches and goes out. Deadly poison, when swallowed, becomes an antidote, or turns into nourishment. Murderers who come intending to kill become like servants. A snare that has been stepped on does not close.
mil5.2.4:10.1: Your majesty, have you heard it said that a hunter, for seven hundred years, was unable to set his snare for a peacock that had performed protection, but set the snare for one that had not done so on that very day?”
mil5.2.4:10.2: “Yes, venerable sir, it has been heard; that report has spread through the world with its devas.”
mil5.2.4:10.3: “Then, your majesty, the statement ‘The practice of protection and medicine is pointless’ is false.
mil5.2.4:11.1: Your majesty, have you heard it said that a demon, guarding his wife, put her in a casket, swallowed it, and kept her in his belly; and a certain sorcerer entered the demon’s mouth, took his pleasure with her, and when the demon found out, he vomited up the casket and opened it, and as the casket was opened, the sorcerer left as he pleased?”
mil5.2.4:11.2: “Yes, venerable sir, it has been heard; that report too has spread through the world with its devas.”
mil5.2.4:11.3: “Was not that sorcerer freed from capture by the power of protection, your majesty?”
mil5.2.4:11.5: “Then, your majesty, the power of protection exists.
mil5.2.4:12.1: Your majesty, have you heard it said that another sorcerer, having committed an offence with the chief queen in the inner palace of the king of Bārāṇasī and been caught, vanished in an instant by the power of a spell?”
mil5.2.4:12.3: “Was not that sorcerer freed from capture by the power of protection, your majesty?”
mil5.2.4:12.5: “Then, your majesty, the power of protection exists.
mil5.2.4:13.2: “It guards some, your majesty, and not others.”
mil5.2.4:13.3: “Then, Venerable Nāgasena, protection is not useful for all.”
mil5.2.4:13.4: “Your majesty, does food guard the life of everyone?”
mil5.2.4:13.5: “It guards some, your majesty, and not others.”
mil5.2.4:13.7: “Because, venerable sir, some people overeat that very food and die of cholera.”
mil5.2.4:13.8: “Then, your majesty, food does not guard the life of everyone?”
